facts.fact: The Inspector-General of Police said on 3 August 2020 that the web-based digital Occurrence Book was installed in all police stations in Nairobi, with more than 10,000 iPads issued to officers, and called it a successful pilot project in Nairobi; no number of stations is given, and officers were given 18 months to move to the system.

The digitisation launched at BuruBuru Police Station, Nairobi, on 3 August 2020 starts with the Occurrence Book, in which all incidents and complaints are recorded; complainants are to receive their OB number by SMS.

The system's developer said on 3 August 2020 that the digital OB is web-based, with data saved on servers and open only to registered officers, and the Interior Cabinet Secretary said seniors track the progress of each complaint in real time.
Capital News states at the launch on 3 August 2020 that police stations have been filing records and all complaints manually, the digital OB then being installed in Nairobi's stations only.

The digital OB was launched on 3 August 2020 by the Interior Cabinet Secretary with the ICT Cabinet Secretary and the Inspector-General of Police, as a National Police Service system built with the ICT Ministry; no funder or budget is stated.
